newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius index edges up, foreigners raise volume.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius index edges up, foreigners raise volume.

text.p: The Mauritius bourse index, Semdex, edged up by 0.52 points to 369.42 with foreign investors seen increasing the trading volume on Wednesday, bourse officials said.

Volume was provisionally posted at 11.06 million rupees on 404,024 shares from 9.34 million rupees on 535,526 shares on Monday. The Mauritius bourse official market opens on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays.

Brokers said foreign investors traded in leading stocks -- Mauritius Commercial Bank, State Bank of Mauritius and New Mauritius Hotels -- which accounted for three quarters of Wednesday's total volume.

Mauritius Commercial Bank was unchanged at 85.50 rupees on 53,977 shares, State Bank was stable at 11.10 rupees on 179,400 shares and New Mauritius Hotels gained 40 cents to 33.50 rupees on 55,770 shares.

"It's the usual trading by foreign investors in these specific blue chips and it saved the day during today's session," one broker said. "If there were not the foreigners, things would have otherwise been quiet in a market which is still looking for fresh news."
The market ended generally mixed and higher share prices of index heavyweights New Mauritius Hotels and conglomerate Rogers led the Semdex up, bourse officials said.

Mauritius Oil Refineries was 20 cents down to 10 rupees on 18,150 shares and Happy World Foods lost 20 cents to 16.40 rupees on 1,165 shares. Fincorp Investment climbed 1.0 to 81 on 1,600 shares and National Investment Trust added 10 cents to 13.10 rupees on 10,770 shares.
Sugar-based companies Mon Tresor Mon Desert eased 20 cents to 41.30 rupees on 2,140 shares and Savannah (ordinary) fell 5 rupees to 140 on 1,025 shares.
Oil concern Shell (Mauritius) was 10 cents down to 16.40 rupees on 4,440 shares and national airline Air Mauritius was unchanged at 44.20 rupees on 1,370 shares.
